summary: logger-libs ships an obfuscated staged exec loader reachable from its public import API
details: logger_libs/_compat.py hides the `exec` builtin behind a chr()-concatenated lookup (`getattr(builtins, chr(101)+chr(120)+chr(101)+chr(99))`) and re-exports it under innocuous names (`see_namespace`, `_install`, `load_module`). logger_libs/helper.py — reachable via the documented `from logger_libs.helper import LogHelper` entry point — imports requests, subprocess, sys, os, and wintypes at module-import time, then reassembles ordered string fragments from generated `.ansi.*` and `.themes.theme_###` submodules, base64-decodes and XOR-decrypts them with hardcoded keys, and passes the resulting Python source to the hidden `exec` with a namespace pre-populated with `url`, `requests`, `subprocess`, `sys`, `os`, and `wintypes`. In this sdist the ansi/themes shards are absent so the decrypted buffer is empty, but the loader harness, the identifier obfuscation, the split-across-submodules payload staging, and the network+shell primitives pre-bound into the exec namespace are the fingerprint of a staged remote-code-execution dropper that executes attacker-chosen Python the moment a release ships the shard submodules. There is no legitimate reason for a logging utility to obfuscate the name of `exec`, split payloads across theme submodules, or pre-wire requests/subprocess into an exec namespace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
